title: NOW I AM READY TO DIE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Israel said to Joseph, 'Now I am ready to die, since I have seen for myself that you are still alive.'" — Gen 46:30 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"Now I am ready to die." That is not despair. It is deep contentment. The one thing Jacob still needed, he has received. Whatever comes now, he is at peace.

There is an old man in the New Testament who says something very similar. Simeon, holding the infant Jesus in the temple, said, "Sovereign Lord, as you have promised, you may now dismiss your servant in peace. For my eyes have seen your salvation" (Lk 2:29-30). He had been waiting his whole life, and now he could go.

Both men found their peace in seeing. Jacob saw his son alive. Simeon saw the Son of God.

Most of us have a list of things we feel we must see or settle before we could ever be at peace. Some of them we will get. Some we will not. But the deepest kind of contentment is not built on outcomes at all — it is built on having seen Christ and knowing that He is enough.

Paul, in a prison cell, wrote that he had learned to be content in any situation (Phil 4:11-13). Not because everything worked out, but because Christ was his.

If Christ is yours, you already have the thing that makes a life complete.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What do you feel you must see or settle before you could be at peace?
2. Where does your contentment actually rest — in outcomes, or in Christ?
3. What would it look like to be genuinely at peace today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, teach me contentment that does not depend on how things turn out. My eyes have seen Your salvation in Christ, and He is enough. Amen.
